Assigned Compute resources - the list of hypervisors (compute resources) assigned to the zone. Unassigned Compute resources - the list of hypervisors (compute resources) in the cloud that are not assigned to the zone. This list depends on the compute zone type. Only hypervisors (compute resources) that can be assigned to a compute zone of this type, will be shown here. For the details, see Zone types. To add a hypervisor (compute resource) to a compute zone When adding several hypervisors (compute resources) to a zone, you can arrange the machines running on particular hypervisors (compute resources) into a paid service. Besides, adding several hypervisors (compute resources) into one zone provides the failover capabilities to your services. Only hypervisors (compute resources) of relevant type can be added to a zone. For more information, refer to Zone types. When you add a hypervisor (compute resource) to a compute zone, the hypervisor (compute resource) inherits the zone’s type. Virtuozzo Server 9 and CentOS 7 hypervisors (compute resources) cannot reside in the same compute zone. Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Zones icon.

title: Managing default CPU quota
content: Managing default CPU quota CPU quota is a percentage value limiting maximum VM CPU load on a hypervisor (compute resource). CPU quota functionality allows limiting CPU usage for the particular virtual machine order to avoid abuse usage, which is affecting all virtual machines on the KVM hypervisor (compute resource). This option is available for the users under administrator’s role. Make sure you have enabled the Manage CPU quota permission first. This feature is available only for KVM hypervisor (compute resource). Before you enable CPU quota, its value is set to unlimited for all the VMs on this hypervisor (compute resource). You can set the default value of CPU quota on the hypervisor (compute resource) level and edit the custom value on the virtual machine level. To set CPU quota for a hypervisor (compute resource) Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Resources icon. Click the label of the hypervisor (compute resource) you are interested in. On the screen that appears, click the Actions button, point to Resource Options, and select Set default CPU Quota. Move the CPU Quota enabled slider to the right to enable CPU quota and set the default value. Set CPU quota. The maximum value is 99%. Also, you can select the ∞ unlimited checkbox to set an unlimited amount of CPU quota. Click the Save button. If the default CPU quota value is changed or the CPU quota is enabled, it does not affect running virtual machines until they are restarted.

title: Adding and managing currencies
content: Adding and managing currencies By default, the system includes three currencies: USD, EUR, and GBP. You can add more currencies at any time. In this document, you can find information on how to add, edit, and delete currencies. To add currency Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Currencies icon. On the page that follows, click the Add () button or the Create New button. Fill in the form that appears:Name - give the label to your currency. Unit - insert a currency symbol. Code - fill in a three-character currency code that is generally used to represent the currency you wish to add (for example, USD, EUR). Separator - specify a character used to format decimal numbers. For example, 100.99. Delimiter - set a grouping character used to separate thousands. For example, 100,000,000. Be aware that it is prohibited to set the delimiter and separator which are identical. Precision - specify the number of digits after the separator. The Precision parameter is used to display the costs total for a certain period, for example, Outstanding amount, Total Cost, and Payments. Precision for unit - the number of digits after the separator. The Precision for unit parameter is used to display the prices for the resources, such as CPU, Disk size, RAM, IP, Data stores, Disks, Backups, Templates, etc. The precision cannot exceed eight symbols. Format - set how the currency will be displayed in the Control Panel. Use the following parameters: %n - for the digits.

title: Viewing hardware info
content: Viewing hardware info Virtuozzo provides an overview of hardware that is used by hypervisors (compute resources) and backup servers available in your cloud. On the Hardware Info page, you can view information on CPU, RAM, hard disk drives, networks, and other hardware components. You can also create custom fields to provide additional hardware information that you find necessary. In this document, you can find information on how to view and manage your hardware info. Permissions The level of user access to the Admin > Settings > Hardware Info page is controlled under the following permission: See all Hardware Info - the user can see all hardware information on the Settings menu. Any actions on Custom Fields - the user can take any action on custom fields. The access to the Hardware Info page for a particular hypervisor (compute resource) or backup server is controlled under the See all compute resources/See all backup servers and Update any compute resource/Update any backup server permissions. For more information, refer to Permissions. To view hardware info Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Hardware Info icon. On the page that appears, you will see the list of hypervisors (compute resources) and backup servers available in your cloud. Click the Show/Hide button next to the label of a resource to expand/collapse the hardware info box.

title: Dashboard
content: Dashboard After you log in to the system, you can see the dashboard. The dashboard provides resource usage statistics, activity log, and your cloud summary. The sidebar menu consists of the following tabs: Cloud that includes Dashboard, Service Catalog, Appliances, and Components, such as templates, service add-ons, recipes, etc. CDN that contains CDN-related resources and server instances.CDN is an experimental feature. Metrics that provide statistics on the usage of Cloud, Storage, CDN, and other available resources. Admin that allows administrators to manage hypervisors (compute resources), users, billing, notifications, settings, etc. Statistics You can choose the time period (24 hours, 7 or 30 days), for which the statistics will be shown. Resource statistics are represented in the form of bars and charts, which show the following. Resource Used Total Chart CPU Total virtual cores assigned to running VMs (may be higher than active cores if overselling). Total physical cores on all hypervisors (compute resources) configured in Virtuozzo. The points on the graph show daily peaks of used CPU (in cores) for a particular time period. Hover over a particular point, to view the peak of used CPU that will appear below the chart. Memory The total amount of memory used currently. Sum total of RAM allocated to VMs + RAM allocated to orphaned VMs. The points on the graph show daily peaks of used memory (in MB) for a particular time period.

content: total of RAM allocated to VMs + RAM allocated to orphaned VMs. The points on the graph show daily peaks of used memory (in MB) for a particular time period. Sum total of all VM disks unused capacities + orphan disks capacities. The points on the graph show daily peaks of used storage space (in GB) for a particular time period. Hover over a particular point, to view the peak of used storage space that will appear below the chart. title: Data store settings
content: Data store settings Data stores provide disk space for your virtual machines and operating systems. Data stores are attached to hypervisors (compute resources). The basic management tools are the same for all data store types, but the creation process differs. This section provides information on how to create, edit, and delete data stores. Data stores have types they inherit from the zone to which they belong. Later, data stores can be attached to a hypervisor (compute resource)/compute zone of the same type. Data stores can be moved from one data store zone to another, but the zones should have the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types. Use caution when changing data store settings. To use the data store, add it to a data store zone and assign it either to a hypervisor (compute resource) or a compute zone. A QCOW2 data store can be assigned only to the Virtuozzo Server 9 hypervisor (compute resource) where it is located. To create a QCOW2 data store Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Data Stores icon. Click the Create Data Store button in the lower-right corner and fill in the following: Step 1 of 2. Properties Label - enter the data store label. Data store type - select qcow2. Enabled - move the slider to the right to turn on the data store. If disabled, new disks are forbidden to be created automatically on the data store.

title: Data store settings
content: select qcow2. Enabled - move the slider to the right to turn on the data store. If disabled, new disks are forbidden to be created automatically on the data store. It prevents the data store from becoming too full and the automatic creation of root disks on particular data stores (high speed, etc.). Click Next. Step 2 of 2. Resources QCOW2 path - for a shared QCOW2 data store (Storage), specify a QCOW2 path to the directory where you mount the cluster. When creating a local QCOW2 data store, prepare a disk, as in the example below, and make the directory on the corresponding hypervisor (compute resource). The hypervisor (compute resource) disk is /dev/sdb, and the QCOW2 path is /hv2/local_storage. title: Managing virtual machine disks
content: Managing virtual machine disks Virtual machine storage is provided by disks. A disk is a partition of a data store that is allocated to a specific virtual machine. Disks can be assigned as the standard or swap disks (there are no swap disks for Windows-based templates). They can also be set as primary (that is, the disk from which an OS will boot). Managing disks for the entire cloud is handled through the Control Panel’s Settings menu. Disks for individual virtual machines are managed through the Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu, where you can: Add disks to a virtual machine Edit virtual machine disks Migrate virtual machine disks Assign a disk to a VM Delete virtual machine disks Do not create multiple partitions on one disk for virtual machines. Control Panel supports only one partition per disk. In cases when you change disk partition, the CP might lose control of such a disk and the VM associated with it. If required, create additional disks instead. Add disks to virtual machines Adding a disk to a virtual machine will require that VM should be rebooted. If a VM is running when you try to add a new disk to it, you’ll be asked to confirm the reboot. To add a disk to a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click a VM’s label to open its details screen. Go to the Storage > Disks tab. Click the Add button () or the Create Disk button in the lower-right corner. Fill in the details:Specify disk label.

title: Managing virtual machine disks

Choose the data store to create a disk on from the drop-down list. Move the slider to the right to specify the desired disk size.The disk size should not exceed 2 TB when a new disk is added. You can later resize the disk if you need it to be larger than 2 TB. Resizing disks to a value larger than 2 TB is not supported for Windows VMs and all VMs on KVM. Virtuozzo provides support only for the MS-DOS partition table. If your disk size exceeds 2 TB, the MS-DOS partition table can be changed to GUID Partition Table (GPT) from inside a virtual machine and extended to more than 2 TB. However, such disks will be partially manageable by Virtuozzo and the subsequent resizing operations will not be supported anymore and could lead to data loss. Move the Hot Attach slider to the right if you want to enable the hot adding of a disk. In this case, a virtual machine is not stopped when the disk is added.To run hot attach, a virtual machine template should support VirtIO virtualization. The hot attach option is available only on KVM hypervisors (compute resources) based on CentOS 6.x/7.x for virtual machines with VirtIO support. Move the Swap Space slider to the right if this disk is swap space. Move the Require Format Disk slider to the right if this disk requires formatting.

title: Managing hypervisors (compute resources)
content: Managing hypervisors (compute resources) Hypervisors (compute resources) are based on KVM virtualization and run with Virtuozzo Server 9 or CentOS 7 as a management operating system. Hypervisors (compute resources) are used to provide hardware resources for virtual machines, ensuring highly-efficient use of available hardware and complete isolation of virtual machine processes. Hypervisors (compute resources) can be organized into compute zones, which make it easy to offer tiered service levels and create private clouds for specific users. Each virtual machine in the cloud is hosted on a specific physical hypervisor (compute resource) server, from which it receives CPU, RAM, and storage capacity from the data stores attached to that hypervisor (compute resource). In this document, you can find information on how to manage hypervisors (compute resources). For more information on how to manage a specific hypervisor (compute resource), refer to Creating and managing hypervisors (compute resources). Hypervisors (compute resources) can run CentOS 7 and Virtuozzo Server 9. Note the following rules applicable to Virtuozzo Server 9 hypervisors (compute resources): Virtuozzo Server 9 and CentOS 7 hypervisors (compute resources) cannot reside in the same compute zone. Do not apply CentOS 7 backup servers to Virtuozzo Server 9 hypervisors (compute resources). Use only Virtuozzo Server 9 backup servers.

Label - the name of the hypervisor (compute resource). IP Address - the IP address of the hypervisor (compute resource). Enabled - whether the hypervisor (compute resource) is enabled or disabled. If disabled, you cannot create the virtual machines on it, or migrate the VMs to this hypervisor (compute resource). Compute Zone - the compute zone to which the hypervisor (compute resource) is assigned. Operating System - the operating system type of the virtual machines that can live on this hypervisor (compute resource).

title: Creating and managing instance packages
content: Creating and managing instance packages Instance packages are preconfigured CPU/RAM/Disk/Bandwidth packages that can be selected during the virtual machine creation process. You can add multiple instance packages specifying different values for the parameters to suit your customer’s needs. Resources that are not set when creating an instance package (for example, swap disk size) are calculated automatically. Instance packages make it easier for users to create virtual machines. The users simply need to select one of the instance packages available to them in the wizard. However, it is still possible to set the virtual machine resources manually if required. Instance packages apply only to virtual machines created on KVM hypervisors (compute resources). To provide your users with the ability to choose virtual machine resources from the predefined instance package(s), add the necessary packages to the users’ bucket(s). After that, instance packages will appear in the virtual machine creation wizard, on the Resources step. Set up instance packages for cloud To enable your users to create virtual machines using instance packages, you need to perform the following configurations: Enable the instance packages permission. Add instance package(s) to your cloud. Add the instance package(s) to the users’ bucket. Interface configuration. Build virtual machine using instance packages.

Enable the instance packages permission There are two permissions that control how resources are selected during virtual machine creation: Select resources manually on virtual server creation and Select instance package on virtual server creation. You can enable one or both of these permissions for your users. By default, users with the role User have the Select resources manually on virtual server creation enabled. If you want your users to be able to select instance packages during virtual machine creation, you need to enable the Select instance package on virtual server creation permission. Depending on the permissions, the Resources step of the virtual machine creation wizard can be different: If both the Select resources manually on virtual server creation and Select instance package on virtual server creation permissions are enabled, the user will be able to choose whether to create a virtual machine using an instance package or by setting resources manually. If you disable the Select resources manually on virtual server permission and enable the Select instance package on virtual server creation permission, the user will be able to select virtual machine resources only from the instance package(s) available to that user.

If you are adding a custom role, make sure to enable either the Select resources manually on virtual server creation or the Select instance package on virtual server creation permission or both if required. title: Assigning and unassigning IP address from a user
content: Assigning and unassigning IP address from a user You can assign and and unassign IP addresses to users from the network overview page. You can assign and unassign IP addresses from shared networks only. To assign an IP address to a user Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the name (label) of the network from which you wish to assign an IP address to a user. Click the Assign IP addresses button. On the window that pops up, select the following parameters: IP net - select from the drop-down list the IP net from which the IP address should be assigned. IP range - select from the drop-down list the IP range from which the IP address should be assigned. User - select from the drop-down list the user to whom you wish to assign IP addresses. Selection - type in the IP address you wish to assign and click Add. You can assign multiple IPs from the same form by filling in an address in the Selection field, clicking Add, and repeating the process for all the required IPs. You can assign a range of IPs by typing them in one of the following formats: 192.168.128.11-20, 192.168.128.11-192.168.128.20, or 192.168.128.11/30. If one or several IPs from the range are assigned to a different user or to VMs that do not belong to the required user, the IP range will not be assigned. The IP addresses and ranges that are to be assigned appear in the IP Addresses field.

title: Assigning and unassigning IP address from a user
content: do not belong to the required user, the IP range will not be assigned. The IP addresses and ranges that are to be assigned appear in the IP Addresses field. If you wish to modify an address or range, select it in the IP Addresses field, make the necessary changes in the Selection field and click Modify. IP Addresses - IPs and ranges that are to be assigned. You can remove the unnecessary addresses or ranges by selecting them and clicking Remove.Currently, assigning multiple IPs to a user works only with IPv4. Click the Assign button. To unassign an IP address from a user Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the name (label) of the network from which you wish to unassign an IP address. Click the Unassign IP addresses button. On the window that pops up, select the following parameters:User - select from the drop-down list the user/s from which you wish to unassign the IP address. IP addresses - select from the drop-down list one or more IP addresses you wish to unassign from a user. Click the Unassign button.

title: Creating and managing IP nets
content: Creating and managing IP nets IP nets contain the IP address ranges of the network. You can add new IP nets to the network, edit and delete the existing nets, and add and edit IP ranges in the IP nets. For information on how to add IP ranges to IP nets, refer to IP ranges. You can add IP nets only to shared networks. To add an IP net to a network Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network to which you want to add an IP net. On the page that loads, click the New IP Net button. Fill in the details of the new IP net:Label - the name of the IP net. Network address - the network address of the IP net. Network mask - the network mask. Must be less or equal to 32. Default gateway - the default gateway to be added to the IP net automatically. Allow gateway to be outside from Ip Net - select the checkbox to allow the gateway to be outside from the IP net. Add default IP range - select the checkbox for the default IP range to be added to the IP net automatically. Otherwise, you’ll need to add the required IP ranges after the IP net is created. Click Submit to finish. To edit an IP net Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network which contains the IP net you wish to edit. Click the Actions button and select Edit next to the IP net you want to modify. Edit the details of the IP net:Label - the name of the IP net.

title: Creating and managing IP nets
content: Click the Actions button and select Edit next to the IP net you want to modify. Edit the details of the IP net:Label - the name of the IP net. If the IP net does not contain any IP ranges, you can also edit the following parameters: network address - the network address of the IP net. network mask - the network mask. Click Submit to save changes. To delete an IP net You can delete only those IP nets that do not contain any IP ranges. Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network from which you want to remove the IP net. Click the Actions button and select Delete next to the required IP net.

title: Creating and managing IP ranges
content: Creating and managing IP ranges IP ranges reside inside IP nets and include the IP addresses that are either assigned to a user or/and used by a VM. The IPs that are neither assigned to a user nor a VM are not shown in the IP range list but are available during VM creation. You can add new IP ranges and edit and delete the existing ones. To add IP ranges you first need to create a network and then add an IP net to that network. You can manage IP ranges only for shared networks. To add an IP range to an IP net Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network to which you want to add an IP net. Click the Actions button and select Add New IP Range next to the required IP net. Fill in the start and end address and the default gateway of the new IP range. Click Add to save the new IP range. The Add New IP Range button is not displayed if there are no IP addresses that can be added to the IP net. To edit an IP range in an IP net Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the required network. Click the IP net in which you want to edit the IP range. Click the Actions button and select Edit next to the required IP range. Fill in the start and end address and the default gateway of the IP range. If you edit an IP range that includes used IPs, the edited range should include these IPs after the changes. Click Submit to save the changes.

To delete an IP range Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the required network. Click the IP net from which you want to delete the IP range. title: Managing ISOs
content: Managing ISOs Virtuozzo allows uploading your custom bootable ISOs for recovery purposes. These could be different images for Windows/Linux/FreeBSD or any additional software. As a cloud administrator, you can limit user’s ability to upload and manage ISOs by permissions and in buckets. You can boot virtual machines from your own ISOs or the ISOs that are uploaded and made publicly available by other users. The default maximum size for uploading ISOs from the file system is 1 GB, this value can be changed via Control Panel > Admin > Settings > Configuration > Max upload size in bytes. There are no space limitations for the ISOs uploaded from the URL (except for your disk space limitations). As soon as you boot a VM from the installation ISO, Virtuozzo cannot control any VM components (backups, networks, disks). Be aware that all the contents of the disk might be deleted if a VM is booted from the ISO that installs a new distributive. If you boot a VM from an ISO with the RAM requirement larger than the VM’s RAM, the transaction will fail. If your cloud deployment is not a fresh installation, make sure that permissions on ISOs are enabled. For more info, refer to Permissions. You can upload your own ISOs and make them available to all users of the cloud (the way the templates work in Virtuozzo). After the ISO is uploaded, it is possible to select the Boot from ISO option on VM management screen.

title: Managing ISOs
content: users of the cloud (the way the templates work in Virtuozzo). After the ISO is uploaded, it is possible to select the Boot from ISO option on VM management screen. View ISOs The system provides you with the possibility of viewing ISOs available to you. To view available ISOs Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Templates > ISO list menu. The page that loads, will show the list of ISOs available to you separated into four tabs:All ISOs - the list of all ISOs available on your system. System ISOs - the list of the ISOs that are publicly available to all users. My ISOs - the list of custom ISOs uploaded by the user who is currently logged in. User ISOs - the list of the ISOs uploaded by your users. For each ISO listed, you see the following details displayed: Log status - the status of the last log item of the ISO (complete/pending/failed). Click the status to view the log details for the ISO (available to the ISOs that were uploaded through a URL). OS - the icon that indicates the operating system of the ISO. Label - the name of the ISO. Min memory size - the minimum RAM size required for the ISO. Operating systems - the operating system on the ISO. Virtualization - the virtualization type chosen for the ISO. Actions - click the Actions button to perform the following procedures with the ISO:Edit ISO. Delete ISO. Make Public - only for the images from the My ISOs and User ISOs tabs.

title: Managing ISOs
content: click the Actions button to perform the following procedures with the ISO:Edit ISO. Delete ISO. Make Public - only for the images from the My ISOs and User ISOs tabs. Boot from ISO Share location where ISOs are stored The default configuration is to upload ISOs on the Control Panel server. Then it is required to mount and share the location where the ISOs are stored at CP with all the hypervisors (compute resources). When the virtual machines are booted from the ISOs, the ISO is taken from the hypervisor (compute resource) server. The location is preconfigured in the on_app.yml config file which can be found in /onapp/interface/config/on_app.yml. iso_path_on_cp - specifies the location where ISOs are stored on the Control Panel server. By default, the location is /data. You can change it to any other suitable location. Ensure that this location is shared with the specified iso_path_on_hv location. iso_path_on_hv - specifies the location where ISOs are located on the hypervisor (compute resource) servers. By default, the location is /data. You can change it to any other suitable location with the onapp owner and read/write access. Ensure that this location is mounted to the specified iso_path_on_cp location. Enable ISO permissions If your cloud deployment is not a fresh installation, make sure to enable the following permissions for your Admin and other roles as appropriate: Any action on ISOs - the user can take any action on ISOs.

title: Managing ISOs
content: fresh installation, make sure to enable the following permissions for your Admin and other roles as appropriate: Any action on ISOs - the user can take any action on ISOs. Create a new ISO - the user can create a new ISO. Destroy any ISO - the user can delete any ISO (own, user, and public). Destroy own ISO - the user can only delete their ISO. Destroy user ISO - the user can delete ISOs created by any user, but not public ISOs. Make any ISO public - the user can make public any ISO available to all users. Make own ISO public - the user can make public their ISOs only. Make user ISO public - the user can make public ISOs created by any user. Create and manage own ISOs - the user can create and edit/delete/view their ISOs. Manage all ISOs - the user can manage own/user/public ISOs. Create and manage user ISOs - the user can view/create/edit/delete ISOs created by any user. See all ISOs - the user can view all ISOs. See own ISOs - the user can only view the ISOs created by themselves. See all public ISOs - the user can view all public ISOs. See user ISOs - the user can view the ISOs created by any user. Update any ISO - the user can edit any ISO. Update own ISO - the user can only edit their ISO. Update user ISO - the user can edit the ISOs created by any user. For more info, refer to Permissions. Upload ISO(s) into the cloud Before uploading ISO for the first time, a root user has to create a /data folder in one’s Control Panel.

Once you’ve configured the locations for storing ISOs and enabled the necessary permissions, you can add new ISOs to the system. You can also make your ISOs public so that other users can boot their virtual machines from the ISOs you have uploaded. To upload an ISO file Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Templates > ISO list menu. On the page that loads, click the Upload ISO button at the bottom of the screen. After you upload an ISO to the cloud, it can be found at Cloud > Templates > ISO List > My ISOs tab. The ISOs uploaded by your users are under the User ISOs tab. Note that you should track the Operating System Type option of the hypervisor (compute resource) where the current VM lives.If the hypervisor (compute resource) is set to Any, any ISO that has other suitable requirements is available to boot from. Boot a virtual machine from ISO Once you have shared the location where ISOs are stored and uploaded ISOs into the system, you can boot virtual machines from them using the machine’s power options menu. title: Managing logs
content: Managing logs Virtuozzo logs all cloud management actions that take place on cloud resources, including virtual machines, disks, data stores, hypervisors (compute resources), templates, networks. View and manage logs In the Activity Log table, you can view and manage the log of all transactions in the cloud. To access and manage logs Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Logs menu. The Activity Log table provides the following details: Icon - indicates the status of an action. Ref - the number that you can click to view details of a specific transaction. Date - time when the action was performed. Action - the name of the transaction. Target - cloud resource with an identification number that you can click to view its details.You can view details on target cloud resources that are displayed in bold, indicating that they are available in the cloud. You cannot view details on resources that are unavailable, for example, resources that failed to be created. Dependent - the reference number of the previous transaction on which the current transaction depends. On the Logs page, you can click: Hide Successful Market Notifications to remove from the list actions that were performed successfully. Click this button again to show the full list. Complete, Running, Failed, or Cancelled to filter logs by their status. Failover Processes to view the list of failover logs. See Failover logs. Clean Logs to clear the logs completely.

title: Managing logs
content: Complete, Running, Failed, or Cancelled to filter logs by their status. Failover Processes to view the list of failover logs. See Failover logs. Clean Logs to clear the logs completely. Cancel All Pending Tasks to cancel all tasks scheduled for completion. Cancel All Pending Backups to remove all pending backups. To search for a specific transaction, you can use the search box at the top. You can cancel a TakeBackup transaction, which is running longer and exceeding the time set for a zombie transaction and for virtual machines. To relegate pending transactions to the failed status Hover over the pending status icon of a transaction and click that appears. This option becomes available if the transaction has been pending for the period of time specified in the Settings > Admin > Configuration > Zombie transaction time parameter. You can see transaction logs updated in real time. This is achieved by means of the tail -f Unix command, which causes the tail command to not stop when the end of the file is reached but rather to wait for additional data to be appended to the output.To enhance readability, the following log items are pointed out with color and font size: Remote Server Fatal Executing Rollback Change tracking To view changes that have been made during a transaction, ensure you have the appropriate Resource diff permissions enabled. If the size of certain resources is changed, the logs will contain information about both the current and previous size of the resource.

title: Managing logs
content: have the appropriate Resource diff permissions enabled. If the size of certain resources is changed, the logs will contain information about both the current and previous size of the resource. Change tracking is available for the following transactions: Resize Disk - changes of the disk size. ResizeVirtualServer - changes to a VM’s number of CPU cores, priority value, and RAM size. ResizeApplicationServer - changes to an application server’s number of CPU cores, priority value, and RAM size. ResizeVirtualServerwithoutreboot - changes to a VM’s number of CPU cores, priority value, and RAM size performed without a reboot. ResizeApplicationServerwithoutreboot - changes to an application server’s number of CPU cores, priority value, and RAM size performed without a reboot. UpdateResourcePool - changes to the resource pool’s resources. EditFirewallRule - changes to the firewalls. EditNATRule - changes to the NAT rules. EditIPSECVPNRule - changes to the IPSECVPN rules. HotMigrate - changes to the ID, label, and IP address of the source/destination hypervisor (compute resource) when the VM is online. ColdMigrate - changes to the ID, label, and IP address of the source/destination hypervisor (compute resource) when the VM is offline. title: Creating and managing recipes
content: Creating and managing recipes The recipe is the plugin mechanism used for adding new functionalities to the cloud. Each recipe is a set of instructions that trigger events at certain stages during the execution of certain services/event in the cloud. Essentially, recipes allow inputting code into virtual machines, appliances or the Control Panel server. This enables administrators to use recipes for configuring the server or report on it, thus providing advanced customization options in a standard environment. Recipes run over SSH, and all commands triggered can run on virtual machines, appliances or the Control Panel server. SSH connection is not required for running recipes on VMware virtual machines. Recipes can range from very simple actions to complex multi step automations interacting with other internal and external systems. Virtuozzo OnApp Support will not be able to create custom recipes based on your requirements, or troubleshoot/debug the lines of code within your own recipes via our support channels. If you would like to commission your own recipes but don’t have resources to do it internally, please contact your account manager for a custom quote. Control Panel does not update the status of the recipe if it takes longer than 1 hour to complete the transaction. Recipe use Recipes allow admins to perform the following operations: Perform post script installation. Use post provision installation scripts for third-party applications, agents, etc. Disk reclaiming.

title: Creating and managing recipes
content: perform the following operations: Perform post script installation. Use post provision installation scripts for third-party applications, agents, etc. Disk reclaiming. Update/modify virtual machines and compute zones with script injection. Allow host to spin up custom virtual machines without requiring custom templates. Download, run and report audit tools. Use of recipes brings cloud administrators more control over their cloud environment and allows them to self-maintain such tasks as custom template creation, etc. You can use recipes for Unix (Linux and FreeBSD) and Windows virtual machines, virtual machine templates, compute zones, and the Control Panel server. For details, refer to the relevant sections: Template recipes Virtual machine recipes Compute zone recipes To be able to use recipes in the cloud, you must enable recipe permissions first. Recipe variables The recipes run when the appropriate events are triggered on the hypervisors (compute resources), virtual machines or the CP server. Depending on the object where the event occurs, the recipe runs on hypervisor (compute resource)/virtual machine/CP and contains the variables for that object. When the recipe execution on hypervisor (compute resource) is triggered by the event happening on a virtual machine, then the recipe also contains the variables for the virtual machine object. The same relates to the CP server.

title: Managing virtual machine recovery points
content: Managing virtual machine recovery points Please note that the Recovery Points functionality is experimental. Recovery points are created as a result of virtual machine data replication on a third-party backup service. Integration with the backup service is handled by means of a plugin that you can install to your Control Panel. The recovery point represents a point-in-time full backup from which you can restore a virtual machine. In Control Panel, recovery points become available after you: Attach a backup resource to a virtual machine. Create an auto backup preset and the preset runs according to a schedule. You can also create a recovery point manually after you complete the preceding steps. In this document, you can find information on how to create and manage recovery points for a virtual machine. For the R1Soft backup plugin, you can set the total amount of recovery points that will be created for a virtual machine by the Max recovery points option while creating an auto backup preset. After the maximum limit is reached, new recovery points overwrite the existing ones. For the Veeam backup plugin, you use Retention Policy in Veeam Backup & Replication UI to control the number of recovery points that are retained on a disk. After the specified number of recovery points is exceeded, the earliest recovery points are automatically deleted to retain the new ones. The Recovery Points-related permissions are disabled by default for the User role.

To enable users to access and manage recovery points, edit the corresponding permissions set for the User role. We support the R1Soft 6.12.0 backup plugin. If your R1Soft version is more recent than 6.12.0, we suggest downgrading to this version if possible. To view recovery points Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the desired virtual machine. Go to the Backups > Recovery points tab. You will see a list of recovery points and the following details:Size - the size of the recovery point from which the virtual machine can be restored. Created at - the date when the recovery point was created. State - the state of the recovery point (for example, available, locked, merged, etc.). Resource - the backup resource on which the recovery point is created. To create a recovery point Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the desired virtual machine. Go to the Backups > Recovery points tab. Click the Backup now button. In the pop-up box, select a backup resource and click the Backup now button. After you complete the procedure, the ImmediateVirtualServerBackup action is initiated to create a new recovery point. The log of the action is available in the Activity Log section of the virtual machine.

title: Sysadmin
content: Sysadmin The Sysadmin page provides statistics and tools for a number of system administration tasks. These tools are divided into the following tabs: Sysadmin tools Services Application errors Activity log Control Panel maintenance IP usage report Resource diffs Sysadmin tools Background task daemon Daemon is responsible for executing all background tasks such as: Transactions Backup takers Billing stats updater Cluster monitor Hypervisor (compute resource) monitor Schedule runner To operate the daemon, use the following buttons: Reload daemon – restarts the tasks, and completes all running tasks if their PIDs still exist. Stop daemon - completes any backups in progress, but prevents any more backups from starting; stops all tasks in progress. Start daemon - starts up all the tasks. Check status – shows the PID of the task and its status. Availability check Availability check enables one to see the status of Services monitoring tool and perform the following functions: Reload the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Disable the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Enable the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Check status of the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Clean Redundant Instant Stat - last time redundant statistics were deleted. CDN Sync Runner - last time synchronization between CDN and Virtuozzo Server was performed. SNMP stats runner - last time SNMP statistics were gathered from the hypervisors (compute resources) and virtual machines running in the cloud. There are three levels of SNMP statistics gathering: Level 1 - every 10 seconds. CP gets info about hypervisors (compute resources) uptime/virtual machines’ statuses. Level 2 - every 60 seconds. CP gets info about disk usage, network usage, CPU usage statistics, and the list of virtual machines. Level 3 every 120 seconds. CP gets a list of volume groups and logical volumes. The level values can be changed in the onapp.yml file. Delete old stats - last time when the old SNMP was deleted. Last time started - the last time when the transaction started. title: Configuring resource allocation and prices
content: Configuring resource allocation and prices Buckets enable you to set up resource allocation and pricing separately. They are subdivided into two tabs: Access Control - in this section you configure the resource allocation for the users under this bucket. If you assign a bucket to a user, that user will have access only to those resources which you have added to the bucket. If no resources are added to a section of the Access Control, e.g. compute zones, the user under the bucket will not have access to any of your compute zones. Rate Card - in this section you set up prices for the resources and the amount of resources users can request for free. Users under the bucket will be billed according to the prices you configure in the Rate Card. These tabs are further subdivided into sections that depend on the server types of resources: Virtual - the server type under which KVM compute, data store, network, and backup server zones of the virtual machine type can be created. Other - the resources that relate to the system and do not have a server type. This section includes backup resource zones, template stores, edge groups, recipe groups, and service add-on groups. For convenience, you can duplicate resources from the Access Control to the Rate Card and vice versa. When adding a resource to the Access Control, select the Duplicate to rate card checkbox, and the resource will be added to the Rate Card with no prices and free limits by default.

title: Configuring resource allocation and prices
content: resource to the Access Control, select the Duplicate to rate card checkbox, and the resource will be added to the Rate Card with no prices and free limits by default. Similarly, when adding a resource to the Rate Card, select the Duplicate to access control checkbox, and the resource will be added to the access control with no limits by default. Be careful when deleting or editing resources in buckets assigned to users or user groups and which have been used to build servers, as any changes will affect these servers. For example, if you have a server running on a template and the template’s store is removed from the bucket, the server will remain running but it will not be possible to edit it. Therefore, we advise you to clone the required bucket and make the necessary changes in the cloned version. Configure Access Control Access control is used to manage user’s resource availability. For the newly created bucket, the Access Control is empty, which means that no resources are available to the user to whom this bucket is assigned. To make compute, disk space, or networking resources available, add the corresponding zones to a bucket. If you do not add resources to a section of Access Control, for example, the compute zone, the user under this bucket will not have access to any of your compute zones.

Select the Duplicate to rate card checkbox if you want to set free limits and prices for the resources. Configure a Rate Card Rate Card is used to manage the prices and the number of free limits for resources. For the newly created bucket, the Rate Card is empty, and that means that a user, to whom this bucket is assigned, is not billed for any of the resources in the system. To configure pricing for compute, disk space, or networking resources, add the corresponding zones to the bucket’s Rate Card. If you add a resource to the Rate Card but do not add it to the Access Control, the user under this bucket will not have access to that resource. In case you remove from Access Control a resource on which users under the bucket have running servers, the users’ existing servers will remain as they are, but users will not be able to access these resources to create new servers. If you leave such a resource in the Rate Card, the users’ existing servers will continue to be billed according to the prices you have configured. If you remove a template store or compute/data store/network/backup server zone from the Rate Card, the prices for the removed resource will be set to zero for the servers using this zone(s). Note that if you set the price equal number with a precision of 10 or more (for example, 0.008789062511) the price is saved equal number with a precision of 8 (for example, 0.00878906).

title: Restrictions sets
content: Restrictions sets The restrictions set is a customizable group of limitations. Configure restrictions sets to create a subadmin role, with control over a limited amount of cloud resources. This tool gives cloud administrators more flexibility in limiting resources and operations available to subadmin role(s). Creating a new restrictions set associates a role or number of roles with certain resources’ limitations. The subadmins can only view and control the part of cloud assigned to them by the cloud administrator. Within that part they have admin permissions. However, they cannot view or use the resources of the whole cloud. Previously, the exact list of resources and actions that the users were able to handle in their cloud was defined by the following parameters: Bucket - configures which resources are available to users (for example, data store zones, recipes, network zones, and so on). If none are added, the user will have unlimited resources. Roles/permissions - specifies which actions the user can perform with those resources configured by the bucket (for example, See all data store zones in the cloud, Edit own recipes only, etc.). The restrictions sets add the possibility to tie the user limitations with the user groups. With this new option, you can choose if the particular resources are restricted by the following: Bucket resources - if restricted by buckets, the subadmins will be able to manage only those resources which are added to a bucket.

title: Restrictions sets
content: particular resources are restricted by the following: Bucket resources - if restricted by buckets, the subadmins will be able to manage only those resources which are added to a bucket. If nothing is added, no resources will be available. User groups - if the resource is restricted by user group, the subadmin will be able to handle only the resources owned by the users of their group. subadmins cannot create any new zones or resources. subadmin cannot create roles, therefore, the roles that subadmin requires have to be created by the cloud administrator. Further corrections to user roles can only be performed by the cloud administrator. subadmin’s users have the same permissions as regular Virtuozzo Server users. We recommend that the cloud administrator grants the subadmin full access to all resources excluding the following permissions:Restrictions Resources group Restrictions Sets group Create/update/destroy role Create new zones or resources In this chapter: List of restrictions resources Creating and managing restrictions sets

title: Schedule settings
content: Schedule settings The schedules settings screen provides an overview of all virtual machines’ backup schedules. This section provides information on how you can create, view, edit, and delete backup schedules. Create schedules When you create a schedule, you can set the time when the backup will be taken. Each backup erases the previous backup and a new backup is not scheduled if another auto-backup from the same schedule is pending or running. When a schedule is no longer needed, we recommend deleting it so that the task will no longer run. Manage schedules You can view, edit, and delete a schedule. To view schedules Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Schedules icon to see a list of all schedules on the system along with their details:Date - the time when the schedule was created. Target - the machine for which the schedule was created. Action - the scheduled action. title: Creating and managing service add-ons
content: Creating and managing service add-ons This chapter provides an overview of service add-ons, the management tips, the information on creating your own service add-ons and providing them as a paid resource for your customers. The Service Add-ons functionality allows you to present to your customers additional services on top of your current IaaS virtual machine offering. You can offer features such as Managed Services, Software Installations and components currently not integrated in Virtuozzo Server. Types of service add-ons There are three types of service add-ons - virtual machine, system and user service add-ons. A virtual machine service add-on can be optionally assigned to a virtual machine or removed from it by users upon their desire to use or not the specific extra resources you offer. A system service add-on provides the ability for you to add obligatory services to a virtual machine, template, or OVA, which cannot be removed by an end user. As for a user service add-on, the services are applied to a user that can be run in Control Panel. Create and configure a service add-on Below is the service add-on creation and configuration workflow. title: Creating and managing templates
content: Creating and managing templates This chapter provides an overview on what templates in Virtuozzo are, the management tips, the information on creating your own templates and providing them as a paid resource for your customers. What are templates? A template is a fully preconfigured operating system environment – a tar + gzip archive that contains the root directory of an operating system. A basic template includes the data needed for a minimum OS installation, but templates may also include applications and additional OS components. Virtuozzo templates are used to deploy virtual machines. The Virtuozzo template library includes over 100 VM templates based on various 32-bit and 64-bit versions of Windows and Linux operating systems. Windows templates To create a virtual machine from a template based on paid software, such as MS Windows, you must have a valid license. The system verifies if you have a license before allowing the VM to be created, so before creating a VM you must first upload the license keys you’ve bought to Virtuozzo, or connect to a licensing server. Virtuozzo supports three license types: MAK licensing: the default licensing type applied to all Windows-based VMs. KMS licensing: this is applicable to Windows 2008 and up. User licenses: allow end users to input a license key when creating a VM. For more information, refer to Managing template software licenses. Types of templates There are two different kinds of templates: System templates.

title: Creating and managing templates
content: to input a license key when creating a VM. For more information, refer to Managing template software licenses. Types of templates There are two different kinds of templates: System templates. These are provided by Virtuozzo and downloaded from an online library. They comprise an operating system with the latest set of packages installed. Most Linux templates require 2–10 GB. Some Windows Templates with additional software may require a minimum disk size of 30 GB - for example, win12_x64_std-sqlweb-ver3.2-kvm_virtio. The minimum disk size for new 4.0 Windows templates is 30 GB (40 GB for templates with MS SQL). Custom/user templates. These are templates you create by backing up an existing virtual machine and converting that backup to a template. This allows you to pre-configure virtual machines (for example with specific OS settings, or pre-installed applications) and use the same configuration again and again. For more details on how to create custom templates from a backup, see To convert a virtual machine backup to a template and To create a custom template. The templates with embedded Microsoft SQL have been removed from the Virtuozzo repository. You can use a new template with Microsoft SQL Express in it, which is free to use. If you require a full SQL version, you should build a new template from a base Windows platform. Where are templates stored?

title: Creating and managing templates
content: Express in it, which is free to use. If you require a full SQL version, you should build a new template from a base Windows platform. Where are templates stored? Depending on the configuration of your cloud, new templates are stored at different locations: Configuration of your cloud Storage locations for templates No backup servers In this configuration, the templates will be uploaded to all hypervisors (compute resources). If this template already exists somewhere, the action is skipped. In such a case, NFS or any other sharing service should be enabled between hypervisors (compute resources). Backup servers are available The templates are uploaded to all backup servers. The action is skipped if such a template already exists. In this configuration ensure that some sharing service is between backup servers. Provisioning is performed at backup servers only. If there is more than one backup server in the cloud, the user is prompted to choose to which BS a template will be stored. The following scheme demonstrates the possible template storage locations depending on your system’s configuration: Template store Template store enables you to organize individual templates into groups that can be used as a paid resource for buckets. This allows you to easily create groups of templates which can be added to the bucket. Only those groups which are added to a bucket will be available to a user. For detailed instructions, refer to Template stores.

My template group My Template Groups allow you to create own license groups for your personal/custom templates. The groups cannot be shared amongst the users. Also, for Windows-based templates, My Template Groups provide the possibility to use your licensing type regardless of your bucket. For detailed instructions, refer to Managing my template groups. Installation and update The Virtuozzo template library includes over 100 VM templates based on various 32-bit and 64-bit flavours of Windows and Linux operating systems. The templates library is constantly updated. For detailed instructions, refer to Creating and installing templates. Billing You can set up templates as a paid resource in several ways. Here you can set a price for each individual template per hour.

title: Managing virtual machine transactions and logs
content: Managing virtual machine transactions and logs The system records a detailed log of all the transactions taking place on your virtual machines. The list of transactions logged by the system includes: Provision virtual server Startup virtual server Stop virtual server Resize virtual server without reboot Configure Operating System Build disk Resize disk Format disk Destroy disk Take backup Convert backup Restore backup Destroy backups Destroy virtual server Destroy template Download template Update firewall You can view virtual machine transactions, cancel pending tasks, and cancel a TakeBackup transaction running longer and exceeding the time for a zombie transaction. To view transactions for a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. The details screen for that virtual machine shows recent transactions in the Activity Log section. To cancel all pending tasks Click the Cancel All Pending Tasks for this virtual server button. To cancel a TakeBackup transaction running longer and exceeding the time set for a zombie transaction Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the required virtual machine. On the following page, in the Activity Log section, hover over the icon of the transaction and then click that appears on the icon of this transaction.

title: Managing virtual machine transactions and logs
content: required virtual machine. On the following page, in the Activity Log section, hover over the icon of the transaction and then click that appears on the icon of this transaction.Please note that this option becomes available if the transaction has been running for the period of time specified in the Zombie transaction time parameter, which can be found at your Control Panel > Admin > Settings > Configuration icon. In the dialog box, click Proceed. The rollback is executed starting from the command that has been canceled. You can also view the details of a particular log item by clicking its reference number. The following page shows the log output and the details: Date - time in the [YYYY][MM][DD]T[hh][mm][ss]Z format. Action - the action name. Status - the action status (Complete, Warn, Pending, or Failed). Ref - the log item’s reference number. Target - the action target. Dependent - the reference number of the previous transaction on which the current transaction depends. Started at - the time when the action is started. Completed at - the time when the action is completed. Data Store - the datastore label. Virtual Server - the virtual machine label. Compute resource - the label of hypervisor (compute resource). Initiator - the user who initiated the action. If you want to see only the detailed output, you can hide log info with the arrow button in the upper-right corner.

title: User accounts
content: User accounts There are two types of accounts in Virtuozzo: administrators and users. An administrator account is created automatically when Virtuozzo is installed. Administrators have full access to the system, including managing virtual machines and hypervisors (compute resources), performing actions on templates and backups, and configuring data stores and networks. There can be several administrators in Virtuozzo. Create and manage user accounts User accounts are created by administrators and have access to those actions which are specified by an administrator. The dash [ - ] and [@] symbols are not allowed as first characters of the login name. First name - specify the user’s first name. It can consist of any 1-20 characters. Last name - specify the user’s last name. It can consist of any 1-20 characters. Email address - specify the user’s email. Time zone - select the required time zone from the drop-down box. title: Managing virtual machine advanced configuration
content: Managing virtual machine advanced configuration You can manage your virtual machines at a raw configuration level by editing the XML configuration file available for each VM in your Control Panel. Virtual machines with modified XML configuration are not supported by the Virtuozzo Support Team. Click the label of the desired virtual machine. Click the Actions button, point to Options , then select Edit XML Config . Click the Unlock button to be able to edit the XML file. In the pop-up box, click Yes to confirm your action. Edit the configuration and click the Save button to apply changes. title: Managing virtual machine backup schedules
content: Managing virtual machine backup schedules The schedules screen lists the virtual machines’ scheduled backups. In this document, you can find information on how to manage virtual machine backup schedules. To view virtual machine incremental backup schedules Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. Go to the Backups > Schedules tab or click Auto-backups under the Options section to view incremental backup schedules only. On the screen that appears, you will see the list of backup schedules along with their details:Date - the time when the schedule was created. Target - the machine or disk for which the schedule was created (depending on the backup type). Action - the scheduled action. Period - how frequently the backup will occur according to a period type set in the next step.For example, if you set 2 as a period and days as a period type, the backup will take place at the same time every two days. By default, this field is set to 1. Period type - the backup period: days, weeks, months, or years. Rotation period - the number of backups, after which the first backup will be deleted.By default, this field is set to 1, so it means that the old one backup is deleted after a new backup occurs. If you set 2 in this field, the first backup will be deleted next but one. If you set 4, three most recent backups and the new one will be stored, while the initial one will be deleted.

title: Managing virtual machine integrated console
content: Managing virtual machine integrated console Virtuozzo provides an integrated VNC console that gives users direct access to virtual machines through the Control Panel UI. The noVNC console is provided for virtual machines built on KVM based on WebSockets. Users with the Administrator role can access all virtual machine consoles for support and troubleshooting purposes. The console connects a user browser to a VNC port or VNC WebSocket port available via a hypervisor (compute resource) for the guest console. To access a VNC console of a virtual machine via Control Panel Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the destination virtual machine. Go to the Console tab. OR Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the Actions button next to the destination virtual machine and select Console. For an HTML5 console, click the Re-connect button if the connection is lost. The re-connection to the console runs as follows: If the console runs as expected, clicking the Re-connect button causes disconnection and the console is re-connected automatically after 1.5 seconds. If the console gets stuck, clicking the Re-connect button runs your request once again and re-connects the console without reloading. If the console gets disconnected with a status code and an error message, the console is re-connected automatically after 1.5 seconds.

title: Managing virtual machine power options

Click the Actions button, point to Power, and select Reboot in Recovery . Click the Yes button in the pop-up box to confirm the reboot in the recovery mode. For VMs with password encryption enabled, the temporary login is root and the password is recovery. For VMs with password encryption disabled, the “root” password will be used to reboot the VM in recovery. Windows virtual machines boot from the Linux-based recovery template in the recovery mode. You need to log in as admin via SSH or VNC console and mount a Windows system disk manually. You cannot work with the “whole” disk (like mount -t ntfs-3g /dev/sdb1) while mounting and checking block devices inside the recovery image as the Windows disk is split into partitions. title: Viewing virtual machine statistics
content: Viewing virtual machine statistics For your convenience, the system tracks VM performance and generates statistics on CPU utilization, billing, network interface usage, and disk IOPS. In this document, you can find information on how to view virtual machine statistics. Virtual machine CPU utilization Virtuozzo tracks CPU usage for virtual machines and generates charts that help analyze VM performance. The charts show the total CPU usage for all the cores of this particular VM for a specified time period. The vertical axis shows the CPU usage percentage (CPU percentage is the core-independent quantity). The horizontal axis defines a time period. To view CPU usage statistics Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. Go to the Overview > CPU Usage tab. On the screen that appears, the top chart shows CPU usage for the last 24 hours. The bottom chart shows usage for the last three months (if there is enough data). If there is less data available, the chart will show utilization for the time available. Move the Show in My Timezone slider to the right if you want to show bandwidth statistics according to your profile’s timezone settings. To zoom into a time period, click and drag in a chart. Click the Reset Zoom button to zoom out again. You can filter the statistics by date and time - select the time period from the drop-down menu and click the Apply button.

title: Viewing virtual machine statistics
content: Reset Zoom button to zoom out again. You can filter the statistics by date and time - select the time period from the drop-down menu and click the Apply button. To see what percentage of hypervisor (compute resource) CPU resource a VM takes, go to your Control Panel’s Virtual Servers menu and click the label of the VM you’re interested in. On the screen that appears, the CPU(s)/Shares parameter displays the amount of CPU resource given to this VM. Virtual machine billing statistics Virtuozzo has a record of all the charges applied to your VMs for the last three-month period. If a virtual machine was created less than three months ago, statistics are recorded for the VM’s existence to date. You can view all statistics available, or those for a shorter period by setting Start and End times. The price parameters on this page do not take into consideration the free limits for resources set in the bucket. When generating billing statistics, Virtuozzo takes the last state of the VM during the hour. For example, if a VM was turned on at 6.15 and turned off at 6.59 it will be considered as being off for the whole hour and its resources will be billed according to the OFF prices set in the bucket. However, the VM’s disk and network interface usage can still be billed in case the VM was on during that hour. To view billing statistics for a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in.

Costs – the total due for the virtual machines, network Interfaces, and disks resources at the point of time specified in the Date column. Scroll down to see Total Amount (the total due for the whole billing statistics period). To save as CSV Click the Save as CSV button to download a CSV file with billing statistics for a selected period of time. The download will start automatically after you click the button. The CSV file includes the following information: stat_time - a particular hour for which the statistics were generated. vs_id - the ID of a virtual machine. resource_category - a resource for which the statistics were generated. The resource category can be a disk, network_interface, compute, template, instance_package, and service_add_on. resource_id - the ID of a resource. metric_name - the name of a metric for which the statistics were generated. The metric can be a disk_size, data_read, data_written, reads_completed, writes_completed, ip_addresses, rate, data_received, data_sent, cpu_shares, cpus, memory, cpu_usage, template, count (for instance packages, templates, and service add-ons), etc. usage - the amount of used resources that can be the following:GBs of disk size, Kbs of data read/written, the number of reads/writes. The number of IPs, the port speed in Mb per second, the data sent and received in KBs.

For virtual machines created from instance packages, the resource category is instance_package, the metric name is count and the usage is 1. Virtual machine network interface statistics Virtuozzo tracks network usage for virtual machines and generates charts that help to analyze network performance. To view statistics on network utilization for a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. Go to the Networking > Network Interfaces tab. Click the Interface usage button () next to the network you’re interested in. On the screen that appears, the following charts are available:Instant Bandwidth - the chart shows the average inbound and outbound speed in Megabits per second (Mbps) of data received and sent over the network respectively. The average speed is shown on a per-minute basis for the last 24 hours. Hourly Data Transfer - the chart shows how much data in Gigabytes (GB) is received and sent over the network per hour. The amount of received and sent data is shown on a per-hour basis for a period of time up to three months.

To filter the statistics by date and time, select the time period from the drop-down menu above the charts and click the Apply button. Virtual machine disk IOPS statistics The system tracks IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second) for virtual machines and generates charts that help analyze VM disk performance. The data presented in the chart are for the periods during which the statistics were gathered, typically 3 minutes. To view IOPS for a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the desired virtual machine. Go to the Storage > Disks tab. Click the Actions button next to the required disk and choose IOPS. The following four charts will appear:IOPS for the last hour IOPS for the last 24 hours Data written/read (in Kb) for the last 24 hours Data written/read (in Kb) for the last hour To zoom in a time period, drag the desired columns in a chart. Click the Reset zoom button to zoom out again. To filter the statistics by date and time, select the time period from the drop-down list and click the Apply button.

title: Creating data stores
content: Creating data stores Data stores provide disk space for your virtual servers and operating systems. Data stores are attached to hypervisors (compute resources). Data stores have types they inherit from the zone to which they belong. Later, data stores can be attached to a hypervisor (compute resource)/compute zone with the same type. Data stores can be moved from one data store zone to another, but the zones should have the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types. Use caution when changing data store settings. Data stores provide disk space for your virtual servers and operating systems. Data stores are attached to hypervisors (compute resources). After successfully installing the Control Panel server and hypervisors (compute resources), follow the procedure to set up a data store. To create a QCOW2 data store Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Data Stores icon. Click the Create Data Store button in the lower-right corner and fill in the following: Step 1 of 2. Properties Label - enter the data store label. Data store type - select qcow2. Enabled - move the slider to the right to turn on the data store. If disabled, new disks are forbidden to be created automatically on the data store. It prevents the data store from becoming too full and the automatic creation of root disks on particular data stores (high speed, etc.). Click Next. Step 2 of 2.

Resources QCOW2 path - for a shared QCOW2 data store (Storage), specify a QCOW2 path to the directory where you mount the cluster. When creating a local QCOW2 data store, prepare a disk, as in the example below, and make the directory on the corresponding hypervisor (compute resource). To create a directory on a hypervisor (compute resource) Add the existing disk of the hypervisor (compute resource) to the data store. The hypervisor (compute resource) disk is /dev/sdb, and the QCOW2 path is /hv2/local_storage. Create the QCOW2 path in the hypervisor (compute resource) and mount the disk into the created directory:# mkdir /hv2/local_storage/ # mount /dev/sdb /hv2/local_storage/Copy # mkdir /hv2/local_storage/ # mount /dev/sdb /hv2/local_storage/ Ensure it is mounted successfully:[root@vhs9 ~]# lsblk | grep sdb sdb 8:16 0 100G 0 disk /hv2/local_storageCopy [root@vhs9 ~]# lsblk | grep sdb sdb 8:16 0 100G 0 disk /hv2/local_storage Add the created disk to fstab:# vi /etc/fstab .... /dev/sdb /hv2/local_storage ext4 rw,relatime 0 0 ....Copy # vi /etc/fstab .... /dev/sdb /hv2/local_storage ext4 rw,relatime 0 0 ....

Ensure the configuration is set:[root@vhs9 ~]# grep sdb /etc/fstab /dev/sdb /hv/local_storage ext4 rw,relatime 0 0Copy [root@vhs9 ~]# grep sdb /etc/fstab /dev/sdb /hv/local_storage ext4 rw,relatime 0 0 Ensure that the qcow2 paths equal the path created on the UI side. Do not locate the data store directory on the same disk as the operating system. Place it on separate disks to avoid an out-of-space issue. Ensure you have turned on the drwxr-xr-x (755) permission, giving others the ability to read the directory but without the option of changing it. Disk Capacity - set the disk capacity in GB considering hardware configuration. Local Compute Resource - specify the hypervisor (compute resource) where the QCOW2 data store will be located. Thus, it decreases the connection time between the hypervisor (compute resource) and the data store. When creating a shared QCOW2 data store (Storage), do not specify a local hypervisor (compute resource) in the Local Compute Resource box.
