title: Managing Storage licenses
content: Managing Storage licenses This page describes the process of managing Storage licenses. You will learn to do the following: Install a new license for a Storage cluster. Update the installed license. View the installed license contents. Check the current license status. Obtain the hardware node ID The hardware node ID (HWID) is required to purchase a Storage license. You can obtain the HWID with the vstorage stat --license-hwid command. For example: # vstorage -c stor1 stat --license-hwid ... 3F96.DFF2.EAF6.CE86.DD49.786C.DC01.3D53Copy # vstorage -c stor1 stat --license-hwid ... 3F96.DFF2.EAF6.CE86.DD49.786C.DC01.3D53 A Storage hardware node ID is not the same as a Virtuozzo hardware node ID shown by the vzlicview command. Install the license Along with installing Virtuozzo licenses on all clients in a cluster, you need to install a separate license to start using the Storage functionality. One license is required per cluster. You can install the license from any server participating in the cluster: an MDS server, a chunk server, or a client.

title: Managing Storage licenses
content: the Storage functionality. One license is required per cluster. You can install the license from any server participating in the cluster: an MDS server, a chunk server, or a client. To install a license Use the vstorage load-license command: # vstorage -c stor1 load-license -p XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXXCopy # vstorage -c stor1 load-license -p XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX-XXXXXX If you have obtained the license in the form of a file, you can install it by using the -f option instead of -p and specifying the full path to the license file: # vstorage -c stor1 load-license -f /etc/storlicenseCopy # vstorage -c stor1 load-license -f /etc/storlicense Update the license In Virtuozzo, you can use the vstorage update-license command to update the license currently installed on your server. When executed, the utility connects to the Key Authentication (KA) server, retrieves a new license, downloads it to the server, and installs it there. To update a license Ensure the server where you want to update the license is connected to the Internet. Run the vstorageupdate-license command to update the license. For example, to update a license installed in the pcs1 cluster, execute this command: # vstorage -c pcs1 update-licenseCopy # vstorage -c pcs1 update-license By default, vstorage obtains a new license from the default KA server. However, you can explicitly specify what KA server to use by passing the --server option to the command: # vstorage -c pcs1 update-license --server ka.

title: Managing Storage licenses
content: from the default KA server. However, you can explicitly specify what KA server to use by passing the --server option to the command: # vstorage -c pcs1 update-license --server ka.server.comCopy # vstorage -c pcs1 update-license --server ka.server.com Once you run the command, vstorage will connect to the KA server with the hostname of ka.server.com, download a new license, and install it on your server. View the license contents You can use the vstorage view-license command to view the information on the license currently installed in your cluster. When executed, the utility processes the license and shows its contents on the screen. A sample output of vstorage view-license is given below: # vstorage -c stor1 view-license HWID: XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX PCSSTOR status="ACTIVE" version=1.0 expiration="08/24/2012 19:59:59" graceperiod=3600 key_number="PCSS.XXXXXXXX.XXXX" platform="Linux" product="PCSS" gracecapacity=5 autorecovery=0 autorebalance=0 snapshots=1 capacity=500 replicas=5Copy # vstorage -c stor1 view-license HWID: XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX.XXXX PCSSTOR status="ACTIVE" version=1.0 expiration="08/24/2012 19:59:59" graceperiod=3600 key_number="PCSS.XXXXXXXX.XXXX" platform="Linux" product="PCSS" gracecapacity=5 autorecovery=0 autorebalance=0 snapshots=1 capacity=500 replicas=5 The main license parameters are explained in the table below. Name Description HWID Cluster ID. status License status. For details, see Check the license status.

title: Managing Storage licenses
content: explained in the table below. Name Description HWID Cluster ID. status License status. For details, see Check the license status. version The version of Storage for which the license was issued. expiration License expiration date and time. graceperiod Period, in seconds, during which Storage continues functioning after the license has expired. key_number The key number under which the license is registered on the Key Authentication server. platform Operating system with which the license is compatible. product Product for which the license has been issued. gracecapacity The amount of disk space that data chunks may occupy in the cluster, in percent to the capacity limit value. For example, if the capacity limit is set to 1 TB, and the grace capacity is 5%, data chunks may use 50 GB above the capacity limit. capacity The total amount of disk space, in GB, data chunks may occupy in the cluster. To view the disk space currently used by chunks, run the vstorage top command, select the V key on your keyboard, and check the FS field. replicas Maximum number of replicas a data chunk may have. autorecovery Denotes whether the auto-recovery feature is enabled (1) or disabled (0). autorebalance Denotes whether the auto-rebalance feature is enabled (1) or disabled (0). snapshots Denotes whether the snapshots feature is enabled (1) or disabled (0).

content: auto-rebalance feature is enabled (1) or disabled (0). snapshots Denotes whether the snapshots feature is enabled (1) or disabled (0). Check the license status You can check the status of your license in one of the following ways: Using the vstorage view-license, for example: # vstorage -c stor1 view-license | grep status status="ACTIVE"Copy # vstorage -c stor1 view-license | grep status status="ACTIVE" Using the vstorage stat or vstorage top command, for example: # vstorage -c stor1 stat | grep License connected to MDS#1 License: PCSS.XXXXXXXX.XXXX is ACTIVECopy # vstorage -c stor1 stat | grep License connected to MDS#1 License: PCSS.XXXXXXXX.XXXX is ACTIVE The table below lists all the statuses a license can have. Status Description ACTIVE The license is valid and active. VALID The license is valid and can be installed in the cluster. EXPIRED The license has expired. GRACED The license is currently on the grace period, or data chunks in the cluster use disk space from the grace capacity. INVALID The license is invalid (for example, because its start date is in the future).

title: Installing a Storage cluster
content: Installing a Storage cluster The Storage cluster is a beta product. Using several standalone servers, one can create a Storage cluster with additional commands. This product is planned to be completely implemented in the future Virtuozzo Server 9 products. In this version, only CLI setup and configuration of Storage are available, which may be challenging if you have never used Storage before. Contact vhs-nextgen-beta@virtuozzo.com if you need assistance. We highly recommend reading the Storage documentation before following the outlined below instructions on how to install a Storage cluster: Planning Infrastructure for Virtuozzo Storage with CLI Management Virtuozzo Storage Administrator’s Command Line Guide Limitations and known issues: Storage can only be set without vstorage-ui-agent. Thus, all the functionality coming from vstorage-ui-agent is not available. This version does not support the prepare_vstorage_drive script. To install a Storage cluster Install Storage packages: yum groupinstall vstorageCopy yum groupinstall vstorage Specify MDS server discovery. To specify the IP address of an MDS server manually, create a bs.list file in the /etc/vstorage/clusters/Cluster_Name directory (create this directory if it does not exist) on the server you are configuring for the cluster and indicate the IP address and port for connecting to the MDS server. Use the IP address intended for a Storage network. echo "10.200.200.11:2510" >> /etc/vstorage/clusters/Cluster_Name/bs.

title: Extending your license
content: Extending your license To upgrade from Virtuozzo OnApp to Virtuozzo Server 9, we will need to extend the feature set of your current Control Panel license key. It is completely free and does not require any changes in your contract. To do that: Go to your Virtuozzo OnApp 7 Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the License icon. In the License Key field, you will find the key in the “XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX” format. Send the Virtuozzo Billing Team an email specifying your Control Panel license key and the number of hypervisors in your infrastructure. You can find the email address of the Virtuozzo Billing Team on every invoice you receive from Virtuozzo. If you are unsure, don’t hesitate to contact your account manager. Below is an email example: Hello Virtuozzo Billing Team, I am in the process of upgrading to Virtuozzo Server 9. My Control Panel license key is XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX. I have ten hypervisors in my infrastructure. In response, you will receive confirmation that the Control Panel license key has been upgraded to support Virtuozzo Server 9 compute zones and a number of activation keys for the upgraded hypervisors. With this, you can proceed to the next upgrade step—upgrading Control Panel from CentOS 7 to Virtuozzo Server 9.

title: Upgrading Control Panel
content: Upgrading Control Panel Prerequisites Upgrade your Control Panel (with the name source-CP) to the latest 7.0 version. Deploy new VzLinux 9.x and install a new Virtuozzo Server 9 Control Panel (with the name target-CP) either in interactive or unattended mode. Ensure your source-CP does not have unsupported features; otherwise, it will not allow you to perform the upgrade. Ensure both source-CP and target-CP are in the same management network and can reach each other. Ensure all hypervisors (compute resources) are online before starting the upgrade. The upgrade procedure log must be displayed via STDIN and appended to /onapp/interface/log/production_import_from_7_0.log. To upgrade Control Panel from CentOS 7 to Virtuozzo Server 9 Copy onapp user keys from source-CP to source-CP for the root user: ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_rsa.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAMECopy ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_rsa.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAME Copy onapp user keys from target-CP to source-CP for the root user: ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAMECopy ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAME Generate a new SSH key for the root user and copy it to source-CP: ssh-keygen -b 4096 -t rsa -q -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N "" &>/dev/null ssh-copy-id -i /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAMECopy ssh-keygen -b 4096 -t rsa -q -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N "" &>/dev/null ssh-copy-id -i /root/.ssh/id_rsa.

title: Installing a Control Panel server with the Firstboot Installer
content: Installing a Control Panel server with the Firstboot Installer The Firstboot Installer is a user-friendly interface for installing a Control Panel server. With this system, you can easily set up the Control Panel server and use a log file to track all the logs performed during the installation. After installing Virtuozzo Server, you can proceed to set up a Control Panel server in interactive mode. To install a Control Panel server in interactive mode Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move around the text in the system. In Virtuozzo Server 9.0 Installation, click the Reboot System button. Specify your login and select the Enter key on the keyboard. Enter your password and select the Enter key on the keyboard. In Installation type selection, select Cluster with Control Panel and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice. In Cluster role selection, select Control Panel Server and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice. In Control Panel Configuration, select one or more IP addresses for the SNMP daemon and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice. Otherwise, manually specify one or more IP addresses (separated by a comma) for the SNMP daemon. After selecting or specifying the IP addresses for the SNMP daemon, select OK and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice.

After the system finishes installing the Control Panel server, you will see the following message about a successful installation: Enter your Control Panel via your browser http://Control Panel’s IP address or http://domain name. Install an Virtuozzo OnApp license to activate your Control Panel. Enter a valid license key via your Control Panel. Your default credentials are admin/changeme. You can change a password via Control Panel > Users menu. After you enter a license key, it may take up to 15 minutes to activate the key. Restart the Virtuozzo OnApp service: # service onapp restartCopy # service onapp restart If you add additional hypervisors (compute resources) to an existing cloud, update the authorized_keys file by running the following script on the Control Panel server: # ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub root@HV_HOST_IPCopy # ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub root@HV_HOST_IP From the Control Panel server, enter the hypervisor (compute resource) server from the Virtuozzo OnApp user via SSH to add it to .ssh/known_hosts: su onapp ssh root@HV_HOST_IPCopy su onapp ssh root@HV_HOST_IP Perform the following Step 13 if you do not plan to install a dedicated backup server. Mount the locations for templates and backups.

For this, add the repositories to /etc/exports on the Control Panel server and then restart the NFS service: # /onapp/templates 192.168.10.0/24(rw,no_root_squash) # /onapp/backups 192.168.10.0/24(rw,no_root_squash)Copy # /onapp/templates 192.168.10.0/24(rw,no_root_squash) # /onapp/backups 192.168.10.0/24(rw,no_root_squash) After the configuration is completed, Control Panel will be available in both http and https protocols. For security reasons, we recommend either closing port 80 or opening port 443. This port is used for secure web browser communication. Data transferred across such connections are highly resistant to interception. Moreover, the identity of the remotely connected server can be verified with significant confidence. If you use a time zone with 30-minute or 45-minute offsets, you need to modify the configuration file /etc/crontab and change the startup time (rake vm:generate_hourly_stats) from 0 to 30th or 45th minute, depending on a time zone.

When virtual machines are booted from ISOs, the ISO image is taken from the hypervisor (compute resource) server. The location is preconfigured in the onapp.yml config file: iso_path_on_cp - specifies the location where ISOs are stored on the Control Panel server. By default, the location is /data. title: Migrating virtual machines from CentOS 7 compute zones
content: Migrating virtual machines from CentOS 7 compute zones You can use only cold migration to migrate virtual machines from CentOS 7 compute zones to Virtuozzo Server 9 compute zones. Cold migration enables you to migrate virtual machines with or without disks and NICs between hypervisors (compute resources) with local storage or across compute zones. Prerequisites You can cold migrate a virtual machine NIC to a VXLAN/VLAN management network that is not shared by the source and destination hypervisors (compute resources). When migrating a NIC to another network, only one IP address assigned to a virtual machine is migrated. The bandwidth from a hypervisor (compute resource) to a hypervisor (compute resource) must be sufficient to transfer virtual machines. Cold migration applies to virtual machines with local storage. Be aware that migration will take longer if you want to perform it between shared data stores. All virtual machine backups made before the migration will become orphans and will not be migrated. You can either delete or convert them to templates. The decision on action to be taken rests solely with you. To cold migrate a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the desired virtual machine. Click the Actions button, point to Options, and select Migrate Virtual Server. In Migration Type: Migration Type - select Full Migrate (Cold). Migrate Storage - turn on the toggle.

title: Migrating virtual machines from CloudBoot hypervisors (compute resources)
content: Migrating virtual machines from CloudBoot hypervisors (compute resources) Virtual machines can be hot or cold migrated between zones despite the template support. Prerequisites Prepare a static compute zone with at least one static hypervisor (compute resource), joined network, and joined datastore. Ensure the user can access both source and target resources in their bucket. If hypervisors (compute resources) among source and target hypervisors (compute resources) do not have a direct network connection, link them by a separate backup network. If you do not have free servers to build a new static compute zone, remove and reinstall CloudBoot hypervisors (compute resources) to a static hypervisor (compute resource) one by one. title: Creating compute zones
content: Creating compute zones Compute zones can be used to create different tiers of service and have data stores and networks attached to them. The combination of hypervisor (compute resource), data store, and network groups can be used to create private clouds for customers. Compute zones have types which are inherited by the hypervisors (compute resources) in the zone. Use Virtuozzo Server templates to build virtual machines only on Virtuozzo Server hypervisors (compute resources). You can keep using legacy templates in legacy compute zones. To add a virtual compute zone Use only the Extended CPU Configuration option for the CPU model configuration in the Beta version. Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Zones icon. Click the Create Compute Zone button () or the Create Compute Zone button in the lower-right corner. On the screen that follows the parameters you need to input depend on the type of the compute zone you want to create: Label - give your compute zone a name. Server type - choose the server type from the drop-down box. Choose the virtual server type to create a KVM zone.The zone’s type cannot be changed after the zone is created. Release resource type - this option allows you to free up the hypervisor (compute resource) resources and over-commit RAM, CPU, and CPU shares by means of the virtual machines that are shut down. By default, the compute zone is created with the Memory Guarantee option enabled.

title: Creating compute zones
content: and over-commit RAM, CPU, and CPU shares by means of the virtual machines that are shut down. By default, the compute zone is created with the Memory Guarantee option enabled. In this case, the over-committing cannot be used.Memory guarantee - the actual free hypervisor (compute resource) memory is calculated. All virtual machines residing on the hypervisor (compute resource) will be able to start.Select only the Memory guarantee option for Release resource type in the Beta version. Max VS to start at once - specify the maximum number of virtual machines that can be started simultaneously on a hypervisor (compute resource) (5 recommended). This option ensures that virtual machines with VIP status will be booted prior to other machines. Placement type - specify the hypervisor (compute resource) selection algorithm, which will be used on virtual machine provisioning and recovery, per compute zone.Select only the Take HV with maximum free RAM (Sparse) option for Placement type. Take HV with maximum free RAM (Sparse) - set this type to select the hypervisor (compute resource) with maximum free RAM during the VM recovery. This option allows you to perform faster migration of virtual machines with a lesser (sparse) number of iterations during the failover. This option behaves in different ways, depending on the event:On provisioning, the round-robin algorithm will be used on hypervisor (compute resource) selection.

title: Creating compute zones
content: behaves in different ways, depending on the event:On provisioning, the round-robin algorithm will be used on hypervisor (compute resource) selection. On recovery, the hypervisor (compute resource) with maximum free RAM will be selected. Failover timeout - the time period for which the iterations will run during the failover if the hypervisor (compute resource) does not respond. CPU units - set the number of CPU units that will be assigned to each hypervisor (compute resource) in this zone by default. CPU guarantee - move the slider to the right to ensure there is enough CPU on the compute zone to create a new VM. Run sysprep - move the slider to enable Windows virtual machine deployment with running sysprep. If there are several simple deployed virtual machines from the same template in the cloud, having identical SIDS, joined to the Active Directory Domain, it will provoke the system conflict. Custom Config - specify any custom commands you want to run when a compute zone is booted. Hot Migration Options Auto-converge - select the preferable type of the auto-converge functionality:Minor - auto-converge with default CPU throttling during migration. Moderate - auto-converge with moderate CPU throttling. Aggressive - auto-converge with aggressive CPU throttling.Hot Migration Options are not available when selecting Virtual Private Cloud server type. After you fill in all the parameters, click the Save button.
